turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. I came in today because... well, I just can't keep my mind on my actual experiments at work anymore. I work as a physical scientist, and lately, my focus is just completely gone. 

If I'm on an important grant call or sitting in a safety meeting, I'll get completely derailed by the smallest things. I'll notice a pump vibration in the lab, or hear a student's side comment, or even just remember some odd peak in an old data spectrum. Next thing I know, I'm off chasing that tiny detail for hours, while the actual project everyone needs from me just falls apart. It's becoming a really serious problem, and I need to figure out what's going on.

symptom_reasoning.S039: The patient reports that their attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli, causing them to chase tiny details for hours.

Yeah, my sleep has definitely changed. Most nights I'm only getting maybe two or three hours... I'll often just fall asleep right on the couch with my laptop still open. 

But I don't feel tired at all. I wake up feeling completely sharp and ready to get right back to work. Honestly, lately it just feels like sleep is an inefficient interruption to everything I'm trying to do.

I just have so much energy for it. Honestly, sitting still right now just feels like I'm wasting the one chance I have to finally fix everything.
